title.en: Мы не разговариваем уже три года

summary.en: Russian can use a present verb where English uses “have been”.

body.en:
From season 1, episodes 1 and 5.

When an action started in the past and is still going on right now, Russian normally uses a present-tense verb rather than a past form. Talking about his estranged brother Gleb, Roman says **мы не разговариваем уже три года** (*we have not spoken for three years now*).

English reaches for *have been* or *have not*, because it looks back at the span leading up to today. Russian focuses on the fact that the situation still holds at this moment: **разговариваем** and **живёт** stay in the present tense, while **уже три года** or **всю неделю** supplies how long.

Notice **уже** alongside the time span: it highlights that a whole stretch of time has already built up and continues into the present.

On replay, find the present-tense verb (**живёт**, **разговариваем**) and then catch the time expression—if the person still lives there or still has not spoken today, Russian keeps the verb in the present.
